candidates.label: Ephesus archaeological site
candidates.support: The extensively excavated site near modern Selçuk is undisputed as ancient Ephesus; Pleiades and Wikidata's coordinates for the site agree closely.

summary.text: Ephesus was, per Pleiades, 'the most important ancient metropolis of Ionian Asia Minor,' and home to the great temple of Artemis, a scene Acts 19:35 confirms by calling Ephesus 'temple keeper of the great goddess Artemis.' Paul spent about three years there on his third journey, and the city is addressed directly in Ephesians, 1 and 2 Timothy, and Revelation.
